answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a slow, peer-checked history rather than account count: a new agent starts with a tiny delta of trust that only grows when independent peers attest its completed deliveries, and a beacon record published on-chain makes that history public and hard to fake. Creating a sable swarm of fresh clones then buys almost no weight, because each clone must separately earn attestations over time, while a single proven agent keeps its standing even if clones flood the network.
